purpose: Complete Lightsaber semantic, selector, and recommendation authority using the standard Lightsaber as baseline.

vocabularyPolicy.rule: Every value in any tag-bearing field must already be used by at least one certified feat or talent.
vocabularyPolicy.negativeMechanicRule: Penalties belong in tradeoffTags/comparison text and must not be promoted into positive finalTags.
vocabularyPolicy.ontologyGapPolicy: Mechanics without a faithful existing semantic tag remain structured or plain-text unrepresented mechanics.

lightsaberComparisonPolicy.variantSelectionRule: A variant should outrank the standard only when its actual specialization matches the character/build strongly enough to justify its tradeoffs.

completionCertification.qaCorrection: Short Lightsaber carries ranged/offense_ranged because frozen Phase 3B explicitly certifies thrown capability; this matches the Phase 4A treatment of intrinsically throwable Knife/Spear profiles.

ruleSelectorPolicy.rule: ruleSelectors are structural applicability metadata and must never be copied into system.tags.
ruleSelectorPolicy.canonicalIdentityAliasRuling: Jedi Academy's equipment text says Long Haft Form; the actual feat heading is Long Haft Strike, so Long Haft Strike controls identity and Long Haft Form is retained only as a source cross-reference alias.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Standard-damage lightsaber that improves successive Block checks in a round from the normal cumulative -5 to cumulative -2, but imposes -2 on Deflect checks.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals normal lightsaber melee damage.
rationale.block: Its defining advantage directly improves repeated Block checks.

pros: Repeated Block checks degrade much more slowly: cumulative -2 instead of cumulative -5.
cons: Use the Force checks made with Deflect take a -2 penalty.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for Block-heavy defensive Jedi; avoid elevating it for Deflect-focused characters.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Standard-damage curved-hilt lightsaber granting +1 equipment bonus on attacks of opportunity while wielded one-handed.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals normal lightsaber melee damage.
rationale.attack_of_opportunity: Its explicit special benefit applies to attacks of opportunity.
rationale.precision: It grants a direct +1 equipment bonus to the qualifying attack roll.

pros: +1 equipment bonus on attacks of opportunity while wielded one-handed.
cons: Its special benefit is inactive when the qualifying one-handed condition is not met.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for one-handed Jedi builds that deliberately generate or capitalize on attacks of opportunity.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Defensive lightsaber tonfa granting +2 equipment bonus on Block and Deflect checks; a phrik-laced handle also resists lightsaber DR bypass, but base damage is only 2d4.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It remains an offensive melee lightsaber despite its defensive specialization.
rationale.block: A proficient wielder gains +2 equipment bonus on Use the Force checks made with Block.
rationale.deflect: A proficient wielder gains +2 equipment bonus on Use the Force checks made with Deflect.

pros: +2 equipment bonus to Block checks.
+2 equipment bonus to Deflect checks.
A phrik-laced handle prevents lightsabers from ignoring the weapon's DR.
cons: 2d4 base damage instead of the standard lightsaber's 2d8.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Strong defensive specialization when Block/Deflect reliability matters more than weapon damage.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Lightsabers do not ignore the guard shoto's damage reduction.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No certified feat/talent-used tag precisely represents resistance to lightsaber DR bypass.

source.book: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: One-handed 2d8 lightfoil that may count as Small whenever beneficial but cannot be wielded two-handed.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals normal 2d8 lightsaber melee damage.

pros: May be treated as a Small weapon whenever doing so is beneficial while retaining 2d8 base damage.
cons: Cannot be wielded two-handed.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Choose when a build gains a concrete benefit from Small-weapon classification and does not need two-handed wielding.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: May be treated as a Small weapon whenever beneficial.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No certified feat/talent-used tag encodes beneficial weapon-size reclassification.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Archaic one-handed 2d8 lightfoil that may count as Small whenever beneficial but cannot be wielded two-handed.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.

pros: May be treated as a Small weapon whenever beneficial while retaining 2d8 base damage.
cons: Cannot be wielded two-handed.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Same mechanical niche as the KOTOR-era Lightfoil: Small-weapon-classification utility without two-handed use.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: May be treated as a Small weapon whenever beneficial.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No certified feat/talent-used tag encodes beneficial weapon-size reclassification.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Modern one-handed lightfoil that may count as Small whenever beneficial, cannot be wielded two-handed, and deals 2d6 base damage.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.

pros: May be treated as a Small weapon whenever doing so is beneficial.
cons: 2d6 base damage instead of the standard lightsaber's 2d8.
Cannot be wielded two-handed.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Only prefer when Small-weapon classification materially benefits the build enough to justify lower damage and loss of two-handed use.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: May be treated as a Small weapon whenever beneficial.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No certified feat/talent-used tag encodes beneficial weapon-size reclassification.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Standard 2d8 Jedi lightsaber and comparison baseline for all Lightsaber-category recommendations.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: Its standard role is 2d8 melee offense.

pros: This is the standard itself: 2d8 damage with no variant-specific penalty or specialization requirement.
cons: No variant-specific specialization bonus.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Default/fallback choice when no specialized lightsaber variant has a clearly supported advantage for the character.

systemDesignContext.userProjectRule: Jedi characters start with the standard lightsaber by default when they become a Jedi.
systemDesignContext.recommendationPolicy: A variant should displace the standard baseline only when its positive specialization matches the character/build strongly enough to justify its explicit tradeoffs.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: 2d8 reach lightsaber pike with phrik-alloy haft; +1 square reach, -2 Block/Deflect, and conditional double-weapon functionality with Long Haft Form.

rationale.melee: Its primary attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: Its lightsaber end deals standard 2d8 melee damage.
rationale.lightsaber_polearm: It is explicitly a lightsaber pike/polearm and this tag already exists in certified feat/talent semantics.
rationale.positioning: Its +1 square reach directly changes attack/threat positioning.

pros: +1 square reach.
Phrik-alloy haft resists lightsaber DR bypass.
With Long Haft Form it can function as a double weapon with a 1d6 haft end.
cons: -2 on Use the Force checks made with Block.
-2 on Use the Force checks made with Deflect.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for reach/polearm positioning builds, especially with Long Haft Form; penalize for Block/Deflect-centric defensive Jedi.

conditionalSynergyTags.reason: Double-weapon functionality is conditional rather than intrinsic and therefore is not promoted into unconditional finalTags.

unrepresentedMechanics.note: positioning captures the recommendation consequence, but no certified feat/talent-used tag precisely identifies intrinsic weapon reach.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: The phrik-alloy haft is not subject to lightsaber DR bypass.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No certified feat/talent-used tag precisely represents resistance to lightsaber DR bypass.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: 2d6 archaic lightsaber powered by a special 600-credit external power pack worn on the belt or back and connected to the hilt by a cord. Force applied to the cord, including a disarm attempt, can disconnect it and disable the blade until reconnected.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct lightsaber melee damage.

cons: 2d6 base damage instead of 2d8.
External power cord can be disconnected, disabling the weapon until restored.
sameAsStandard: Uses normal lightsaber proficiency and melee role.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Primarily an era/flavor choice rather than a mechanical upgrade; recommend only when archaic equipment identity matters more than damage and reliability.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: External power cord can be disconnected by force applied to the cord, including a disarm attempt, causing the weapon to become unusable until reconnected.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No certified semantic tag faithfully represents a cord-disconnection vulnerability.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d8/2d8 double-bladed lightsaber. One or both blades can be ignited. With both blades active it is a double weapon and can attack with both ends as a full-round action using normal double-weapon penalties.

rationale.offense_melee: Each active blade deals standard 2d8 lightsaber damage.
rationale.double_weapon: With both blades active it is explicitly a double weapon.
rationale.full_attack: Attacking with both ends uses a full-round double-weapon attack.

pros: Can function as a 2d8/2d8 double weapon when both blades are active.
Supports double-weapon full-attack builds.
cons: Large weapon using normal double-weapon penalties when attacking with both ends.
Requires two special energy cells.
sameAsStandard: Each individual blade deals the standard 2d8 base damage.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for characters explicitly invested in double-weapon/full-attack fighting; otherwise the standard lightsaber is simpler and less specialized.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: One or both blades can be ignited independently.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Blade activation state determines whether double-weapon rules apply.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: 2d8 lightsaber with a swift-action extended mode. Extended mode increases reach by 1 square but imposes -2 Reflex Defense against attacks from adjacent targets.

rationale.offense_melee: Both settings deal standard 2d8 lightsaber damage.
rationale.positioning: Extended mode increases reach by 1 square.
rationale.swift_action: Changing blade length is performed as a swift action.
rationale.action_economy: The reach/defense tradeoff is controlled through an explicit combat action.

pros: Swift-action extended mode grants +1 square reach.
cons: While extended, Reflex Defense is -2 against attacks from adjacent targets.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for positioning/reach builds that can manage the adjacent-defense drawback and make good use of swift-action mode changes.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Extended mode gives +1 square reach and -2 Reflex Defense against adjacent attackers.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: positioning/action tags capture recommendation role; exact defense penalty remains mode-specific.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d10 oversized lightsaber. Only Large or larger creatures can use it in conjunction with feats or talents that affect light weapons or lightsabers, such as Weapon Finesse.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d10 lightsaber melee damage.

pros: 2d10 base damage instead of 2d8.
cons: Only Large or larger wielders can combine it with feats/talents that affect light weapons or lightsabers.
sameAsStandard: Uses Lightsaber proficiency and normal lightsaber DR-bypass behavior.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: High-base-damage option for Large+ wielders; de-prioritize for smaller characters or builds relying on light-weapon/lightsaber feat interactions.

selectorGuardrails: Do not infer `damage_bonus` solely from the printed 2d10 base dice.
Feat/talent eligibility keyed to light weapons or lightsabers is size-gated to Large-or-larger wielders.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Only Large or larger creatures can use the weapon with feats/talents that affect light weapons or lightsabers.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: This is an applicability gate, not a semantic tag.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Small 2d6 shoto lightsaber favored by Small Jedi and often used as an off-hand weapon. The source grants no intrinsic off-hand attack bonus; its major build value comes through shoto-specific abilities.

rationale.melee: Its printed attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d6 lightsaber melee damage.
rationale.ranged: Frozen Phase 3B explicitly certifies the short lightsaber as thrown-capable, so it supports a ranged weapon-use role without inventing a `thrown` semantic tag.
rationale.offense_ranged: Its certified thrown capability permits direct ranged offense; exact thrown handling remains structural.

pros: Small shoto identity enables explicit Shoto Focus and Shoto Master interactions.
Frozen Phase 3B certifies intrinsic thrown capability, giving it a ranged fallback profile.
cons: 2d6 base damage instead of 2d8.
sameAsStandard: Uses Lightsaber proficiency and normal lightsaber DR-bypass behavior.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for shoto/off-hand builds specifically supported by Shoto Focus or Shoto Master; do not recommend merely because flavor text mentions two-weapon fighting.

selectorGuardrails: Do not add `dual_wield` to the weapon itself; the source grants no intrinsic two-weapon bonus.
Do not add a `thrown` semantic tag; thrown capability is structural while `ranged`/`offense_ranged` capture its build-facing ranged role.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: 2d4 reach-2 lightsaber whip. On a hit it can initiate a grab or grapple. A held target can escape with DC 15 Acrobatics; Pin and Trip are allowed, Crush and Throw are prohibited. A target ending its turn held by the lightwhip takes the weapon's unmodified base damage again.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct lightsaber melee damage.
rationale.positioning: Reach 2 squares materially changes melee threat distance.
rationale.grab: A hit can initiate a grab.
rationale.grapple: A hit can initiate a grapple.
rationale.restrain: Targets can remain held by the lightwhip across turns.
rationale.control: The weapon converts hits into ongoing restraint.
rationale.battlefield_control: Reach plus grab/grapple/Pin/Trip options materially limit enemy movement and actions.
rationale.sustained_damage: A target ending its turn held by the lightwhip automatically takes the weapon's base damage again.

pros: Reach 2 squares.
Can initiate grab or grapple on a hit.
Supports Pin and Trip.
Held targets take recurring base damage at end of their turns.
cons: 2d4 base damage instead of 2d8.
Crush and Throw cannot be used with it.
sameAsStandard: Uses Lightsaber proficiency and ignores DR as a lightsaber.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Strong control/reach option for grab, grapple, Pin, Trip, and sustained restraint builds; poor for raw weapon-damage builds.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Held target can escape with DC 15 Acrobatics.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: The target's escape method is not a user-build semantic tag.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: End-turn recurring damage uses only the weapon's base damage and excludes Strength, half heroic level, and all other modifiers.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Exact modifier exclusions must be preserved.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: 2d8 long-handle lightsaber. When wielded two-handed, the wielder may forgo doubling Strength bonus to damage and instead increase base damage to 2d10. Long Haft Strike (called Long Haft Form in the equipment text) conditionally enables a 1d6 haft-end double-weapon mode.

rationale.offense_melee: Its blade provides direct lightsaber melee offense.
rationale.damage_bonus: Its defining special option explicitly changes the base damage profile from 2d8 to 2d10 under a two-handed choice.

pros: When wielded two-handed, can choose a 2d10 base-damage profile instead of doubled Strength bonus.
With Long Haft Strike/Form it can function as a double weapon with a 1d6 haft end.
cons: The 2d10 option explicitly gives up the normal doubled Strength bonus from two-handed wielding.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for two-handed Jedi whose Strength and build make the 2d10 alternate profile favorable, especially if they also have Long Haft Strike.

conditionalSynergyTags.condition: wielder has Long Haft Strike (called Long Haft Form in equipment text)
conditionalSynergyTags.reason: Double-weapon functionality is feat-gated and therefore not unconditional.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Two-handed wielder chooses between normal base damage with doubled Strength bonus or 2d10 base damage without doubled Strength bonus.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Exact comparison depends on wielder Strength; do not treat 2d10 as universally superior.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Haft-end damage type is not stated by the source.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Do not infer bludgeoning or lightsaber DR bypass for the haft end.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: 2d8 corded lightsaber with a three-state output cycle. As a swift action it overcharges to 2d10 until the end of the wielder's next turn, then is forced to 2d4 for one round before returning to normal; overcharge cannot be reactivated during burnout.

rationale.melee: All output states are melee lightsaber attacks.
rationale.offense_melee: All states provide direct melee offense.
rationale.swift_action: Overcharge is activated as a swift action.
rationale.action_economy: Damage output is governed by an explicit action-triggered state cycle.
rationale.damage_bonus: Overcharge explicitly raises base damage from 2d8 to 2d10.
rationale.burst_damage: The weapon offers a temporary high-output spike followed by a forced low-output recovery state.

pros: Swift-action overcharge raises base damage from 2d8 to 2d10 through the end of the wielder's next turn.
cons: After overcharge, base damage is forced down to 2d4 for one round.
Cannot overcharge again during the burnout round.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Burst-damage lightsaber for characters who can exploit a planned damage window and tolerate a forced low-output recovery round.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: State machine: normal 2d8 -> swift-action overcharge 2d10 -> forced one-round burnout 2d4 -> normal; burnout locks out re-overcharge.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Exact transition timing must remain structured.
Construction difficulty is not promoted into semantic tags.
